correctness.rationale: For every proper support, the weighted cycle breaks into path components and each nonzero path run of length r has rank 2 ceil(r/2). The three-state cyclic transfer matrix counts these supports exactly and its two nonzero eigenvalues satisfy the Lucas recurrence with parameter q(q-1)u. For full support, odd cycles always have corank one, while even cycles have full rank unless their two perfect-matching Pfaffian monomials cancel; exactly (q-1)^(n-1) all-nonzero assignments cancel, and those matrices have rank n-2. These cases give the stated formulas. For odd q, the established class-two character-rank theorem multiplies each rank count by q^(n-2i). The packaged checker independently reproduces exact matrix ranks over F2, F3, F4, and F5 in seven cases and verifies the character sum-of-squares identity.

originality.rationale: Rossmann's primary paper explicitly poses the graphical-group character-enumeration problem and lists polynomial solutions for edgeless graphs, paths, and complete graphs, but not cycles. It also identifies antisymmetric rank counting as the relevant route and states that the general effectiveness of that route is unclear. The final theorem supplies a closed rank enumerator for the natural unicyclic cycle family and hence an explicit character-degree formula for odd q. Targeted database and literature searches found no equivalent cycle theorem.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a closed answer for an infinite natural graph family to an explicit character-enumeration problem. Cycles are the first connected unicyclic family after paths, and the even-cycle case introduces a genuine Pfaffian cancellation that is not present in path forests. The result therefore extends the solved landscape structurally rather than by a routine parameter increment, while also producing explicit irreducible-character multiplicities for all odd finite fields.
